title: Flyto2 Core image.download -- T1105 attacker-hosted bytes land outside the sandbox because the path check's base is caller-controlled
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-67429 (GHSA-2956-977x-2w3r,
CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), affecting Flyto2 Core (`flyto-core`)'s
`image.download` module and its file-writing siblings.

`image.download` in `src/core/modules/atomic/image/download.py`
fetches a caller-supplied URL and writes the response to disk. Unlike
`file.write`, which uses the central `validate_path_with_env_config()`
guard confining writes to `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR`, `image.download`
checks its target path against `output_dir` -- a parameter the SAME
caller also controls. Setting `output_dir` to `/` makes
`os.path.commonpath()` accept any absolute target, so the check is
self-defeating: the attacker chooses both the value being validated
and the base it is validated against. The HTTP response body --
fully attacker-controlled bytes, since the URL is only SSRF-checked,
not content-checked -- is then written verbatim to that path.
`image.convert`, `image.resize`, `document.excel_write`,
`document.pdf_fill_form` and several other file-writing modules share
the same caller-controlled-base pattern, though their content is
format-constrained; `image.download` is the strongest because the
written bytes are arbitrary.

Detection logic flags an `image.download` (or sibling file-writing
module) invocation whose `output_dir` parameter is a filesystem root
or a path outside the module's own default sandbox prefix -- the
exact caller-controlled-base pattern this advisory's proof of concept
demonstrates writes attacker bytes outside `FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR` while
the guarded `file.write` sibling correctly refuses the identical
escape.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (flyto-core, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source file, a runnable reproduction
script contrasting `file.write` vs. `image.download` on the same
escape target, and a list of every other affected file-writing
module), fixed in flyto-core 2.26.7+ (verified via live GHSA lookup,
2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's
patch release and understated the CVSS score; this note corrects both
stale claims, not the detection logic itself).
